transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-11
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Olivia (Head of ML, Insightra), Samir (CTO), Leah (Sr Eng), Marco (Security)

Auto-generated summary (may be incomplete): Discussed POC goals and model tradeoffs for multilingual intent/entity extraction across English, Spanish, Portuguese; emphasized latency budget for interactive flows and batch enrichment flows; security asks for KMS and VPC/private deployment options.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, show of hands, is the time still good?
[00:06] Olivia: Yeah works for me, thanks Maya.
[00:09] Samir: Yep, thanks we got the calendar.
[00:12] Ethan: Great cool, quick agenda — goal is to scope a 6-week POC, agree success criteria, pick 3-4 open models to test, and define benchmarks and data needs.
[00:20] Leah: Sounds good. Quick context — Insightra's customer support pipeline is multilingual, mainly EN/ES/PT but also some FR/IT. We want intent extraction + slot filling and named entities, accuracy is primary but we can't exceed 200ms P50 for the interactive UI. P95 can be up to 700ms for now.
[00:40] Olivia: To add, we have daily volume of ~1.2M incoming messages, rated at weekdays, but the POC will exercise a sampled subset — thinking 100k messages over 2 weeks for evaluation.
[01:02] Maya: Nice, that's super helpful. When you say accuracy is primary — are you measuring intent-level F1 or per-entity span exact match?
[01:08] Olivia: Intent F1 is the main metric, target net F1 > 0.88 on our test set. For entities we want > 0.82 exact-match. Those are kind of aspirational for the POC to consider a rollout.
[01:22] Samir: Also cost: production target is under $0.20 per 1k messages after optimization — that's a ballpark.
[01:30] Ethan: Okay good. For model candidates we'll look at a range — big open LLMs, mid-size quantized ones, and possibly custom fine-tuned variants. Tradeoffs: bigger models usually win on accuracy & multilingual, but cost and latency suffer. Quantization can reduce latency/cost but might impact entity exactness.
[01:58] Marco: From Security side, we need SOC2 type II, SSO (SAML), audit logs, and optional VPC/private deployment. KMS for customer keys is non-negotiable if we move outside staging — but for POC hosted is fine as long as logs are retained in tenant-isolated buckets.
[02:20] Maya: Understood. Redwood offers Hosted API for fastest start, Dedicated reserved GPU for throughput, and Private VPC options. For POC we typically recommend Hosted run with strict isolation + customer-managed buckets; if you want to validate Dedicated latency we can spin a small dedicated pool for the benchmark.
[02:41] Olivia: That sounds reasonable. For the POC acceptance criteria — let's be explicit: 1) intent F1 >= 0.88 on our eval set, 2) entity exact-match >= 0.82, 3) average cost <= target (Samir will define), 4) P50 latency <= 200ms and P95 <= 700ms on typical payloads, 5) data controls & SOC2 baseline met.
[03:05] Ethan: Great — we'll capture that as the POC success checklist. Now on models: we propose testing 4 candidates across compute/cost spectrum — a large LLM (higher accuracy), a medium open model optimized for multi-lingual, a quantized 8-bit variant for cost/latency, and a small distilled model for baseline throughput.
[03:30] Leah: Any specific model names in mind?
[03:32] Ethan: Tentative shortlist: LlamaX-33B (open fine-tuned), Mistral-multi-13B, OpenMTL-7B-8q (quantized), and TinySL-3B distilled. Note: names are placeholders — we'll provide exact repos/weights.
[03:50] Olivia: We use spaCy for some pipelines today, but our main comparison is to in-house fine-tuned BERT models. How do these open LLMs compare on entity exact-match?
[04:05] Ethan: Large LLMs tend to do well on intent and few-shot entity labeling; span exact-match can vary. That's why we'll run a targeted entity extraction prompt set plus strict evaluator that checks token spans. Quantized models may drop a few points on entity spans, so we want to quantify that.
[04:25] Samir: Can you explain more about quantization impact — do you have numbers?
[04:28] Ethan: Sure; rough rule-of-thumb from previous POCs: going from fp16 to 8-bit quantization usually changes entity exact-match by 1-4% depending on prompt style and post-processing. Latency improvements are often 20-40% and cost halves or better. But that's model-dependent — we'll run the numbers.
[04:50] Maya: Important note — the UI requires sub-200ms P50 for interactive sessions. For any model that can't meet that on Hosted, we can test Dedicated with colocated GPUs. But Dedicated has lead time — provisioning takes 2-3 weeks typically. For POC timeline of 6 weeks we can do hosted baseline then run a dedicated benchmark in week 4-5 if needed.
[05:15] Olivia: Good flag. For multilingual evaluation, do you recommend synthetic augmentation or sampling from production?
[05:20] Ethan: Best practice is sample production for natural distribution and then augment with synthetic prompts to stress low-frequency languages. For languages like Portuguese we may need extra examples to stabilize metrics.
[05:36] Leah: For workload sizing — Olivia mentioned 1.2M messages/day. Do you have peak QPS numbers?
[05:40] Olivia: Peak about 450 QPS across all regions; typical is ~14 QPS per region but bursts up to 120 QPS per region during certain windows.
[05:52] Ethan: For POC we'll simulate both interactive QPS and batch enrichment (async) patterns. We'll ask for 100k sample messages and a representative latency histogram — that will let us scale the benchmark to realistic peaks.
[06:10] Marco: Regarding data residency — we need EU region processing for EU customers. Is that supported?
[06:15] Maya: Yes, Redwood has region routing and can run models in EU regions. For POC we'll ensure the test data for EU customers stays in EU. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can do on-prem if required later.
[06:30] Samir: A few procurement/security questions: 1) Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS? 2) Can we get raw audit logs for model calls?
[06:37] Maya: Yes on both — customer KMS and audit logs are supported. We'll share security docs and SOC2 report after NDA.
[06:44] Marco: NDA is already in place, thanks. We'll still need a formal security questionnaire answered — I'll send that.
[06:50] Maya: Perfect, we'll prioritize that.
[06:52] 
[07:10] Ethan: Back to benchmarks — proposed experiments for the POC: A) functional accuracy evaluation (intent/entity) on 100k sample, B) latency profile at 1x and 5x POC traffic, C) cost per 1k messages and tokens with caching/batching toggles, D) failure and fallback tests (model timeout, network outage).
[07:35] Olivia: For scoring we want deterministic eval scripts — can you commit to reproducible scripts so we can compare across runs?
[07:40] Ethan: Absolutely, we'll provide a benchmarking harness (docker + scripts) and a spreadsheet with metrics. We'll also version the prompt sets and exact model checkpoints so runs are auditable.
[07:52] Leah: Is there support for running local evals with our in-house data without sending it to hosted env?
[07:56] Maya: We can support an offline runner using the Redwood runtime (private package) in your VPC — that's part of Redwood Private offering. For POC we usually avoid the full Private install because of setup time, but we can provide a containerized runner that runs inference locally using quantized weights you pull from the model hub.
[08:20] Samir: Timeline question — what's realistic for 6-week POC?
[08:24] Ethan: Week 0: kickoff + env/data collection; Week 1: baseline runs on Hosted for 2 models; Week 2-3: full benchmarking across shortlist + tuning (prompt templates, quantization profiles); Week 4: optional Dedicated benchmark if needed; Week 5: run final regressions + cost modeling; Week 6: wrap up + decision. If Dedicated needed earlier, lead time is 2-3 weeks so we'd flag that by end of week 1.
[08:52] Olivia: That timeline works. We have a product review with execs on Feb 25 so if we can deliver a recommendation by Feb 18 that fits our plan (that's within 6 weeks).
[09:05] Maya: We'll align dates — starting next week (Jan 18) would put final recommendation in mid-Feb. We'll note Feb 18 as target delivery.
[09:14] 
[09:30] Marco: Quick question about PII — some messages contain PII, can Redwood redact at ingestion?
[09:36] Ethan: We support pre-ingest masking rules and can optionally run a redaction step in the pipeline. For the POC we recommend Insightra do local anonymization before upload. We can help with a redaction script.
[09:50] Leah: For evaluation we prefer a redacted copy plus a key mapping for evaluation only — we understand redaction may alter tokenization and could affect entity matching.
[10:05] Maya: Good point — we'll note that as a caveat in the eval plan.
[10:10] 
[10:30] Olivia: Let's talk about rollbacks and model fallback policies — we sometimes need immediate fallback to a cheaper model on overload. Does Redwood support automatic fallback?
[10:38] Ethan: Yes — routing policies can fallback based on latency or error rate. You can route 100% to primary then fallback to a smaller model on violations. Policies are configurable per route.
[10:48] Samir: And can we do A/B testing across models for a subset of traffic?
[10:52] Maya: Absolutely — Redwood Console supports canary and percentage rollouts per route and per model version. We'll show that in the console demo.
[11:05] 
[11:30] Olivia: Anything else we should call out?
[11:33] Leah: One more — for multilingual, we want to ensure tokenizers don't split entities oddly across languages. Are you planning to include token-level alignment checks?
[11:40] Ethan: Yes, we'll include token-level and span-based checks for each language. For languages with diacritics we'll add normalization steps.
[11:50] Maya: Okay to recap — Success criteria (intent F1, entity exact-match, latency, cost, security), data: Insightra provides 100k samples plus two weeks of logs and latency histograms, Redwood to deliver model shortlist + benchmarking harness by Jan 14-15, schedule technical deep-dive week of Jan 25, target recommendation Feb 18.
[12:18] Olivia: That captures it. We'll also send a short doc with priority languages and edge-case examples.
[12:25] Marco: I'll share the security questionnaire and expected compliance checklist.
[12:28] Maya: Great. Any blockers?
[12:31] Samir: No blockers. We want to see quick baselines so execs get confidence.
[12:36] Maya: Understood — we'll focus on fast wins first.
[12:40] 
[12:50] Ethan: One more note on cost modeling — we'll show cost with and without KV cache and batching curves, because caching could dramatically reduce token usage for repeated prefixes.
[12:58] Leah: Good — caching is relevant for our templated responses.
[13:04] Maya: Alright, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the model list and the benchmark repo links.
[13:10] Olivia: Thanks all.
[13:12] Meeting end.

Optional attachments referenced: "benchmark-harness-repo (will be shared)", "security-questionnaire.pdf (from Marco)", "sample-logs.zip (Insightra to share)"
